references.text: In Mark's parallel account, Jesus says to the synagogue ruler: "Do not be afraid; only believe!" – almost identical words as in Luke 8:50.
Just before, in the same context, Jesus says to the woman with bleeding: "Your faith has saved you." Faith that saves is a recurring theme in this passage.
Jesus says to the sinful woman: "Your faith has saved you; go in peace." The same connection between faith and salvation (σωθήσεται) as in 8:50.
Matthew's parallel account of the synagogue ruler's daughter. A leader comes to Jesus and asks him to lay hands on his daughter, and Jesus follows him.
Mark's parallel account where Jairus comes to Jesus and asks him to come and lay hands on his daughter who is dying.
"Do not be afraid, for I am with you" – God's call not to fear is a recurring biblical theme, which Jesus here applies to Jairus.
"Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you" – The Lord's words about not fearing, parallel to Jesus' exhortation to Jairus not to fear but to believe.

Jesus says to Martha: "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live even if they die." Faith in Jesus as the conqueror of death, just as Jairus is encouraged to believe that his daughter will be saved/rescued.
The messengers from Jairus' house say that his daughter has died and that he should no longer trouble the teacher – the immediate context that triggers Jesus' encouraging words in Luke 8:50.
The direct occasion: While Jesus was still speaking, some came from the synagogue ruler's house saying that his daughter had died – to which Jesus responds with encouragement about faith.
